title: Fleet Readiness API – proto notes (endpoints + event schema)
body:
Context
- Goal: a small, boring control-plane API that records “readiness state” for GPU nodes + exposes enough detail for infra tooling / internal console to make decisions.
- Source of truth is the control plane (not Kubernetes labels), but it should incorporate agent validation results + orchestration events.
- Aligning with ADR-017 state machine:
  - Allocated -> Provisioning -> Validating -> Ready
  - Failure path: Quarantined (with reason + remediation hint)

Non-goals (for proto)
- Not designing a full event-sourcing system.
- Not exposing this externally to customers.
- Not implementing a full “workflow engine”; provisioning orchestrator remains the driver.


Entities (current thinking)
1) NodeReadiness
- node_id: canonical unique ID (NOT hostname; hostnames churn on reimage)
- provider_instance_id: i-… (AWS) / equivalent
- cluster_id
- pool_id (Dedicated pool)
- region
- gpu_type (A100/H100/L4 etc)
- image_channel: candidate|stable
- image_version: e.g. gpu-ubuntu2204-nvidia-550.54.14-cuda12.4-2025.10.02
- current_state: Allocated|Provisioning|Validating|Ready|Quarantined
- state_updated_at (server timestamp)
- state_version (monotonic int for optimistic concurrency)

2) ValidationRun
- validation_run_id
- node_id
- started_at, finished_at
- overall_status: pass|fail|partial|timeout
- checks[]: each check has name, status, duration_ms, artifact_ptr (optional), failure_reason (optional)

3) FailureReason (normalized-ish)
- code: enum-ish for dashboards (ex: GPU_ECC_HIGH, NVIDIA_XID, DRIVER_MISMATCH, KUBELET_JOIN_FAILED, NCCL_SMOKE_TIMEOUT, DISK_IOPS_LOW)
- message: operator-facing string (safe; no secrets)
- remediation: short suggestion (ex “reimage”, “drain+retry validation”, “quarantine and page networking”)


API design notes
- Internal only; behind service-to-service auth.
- We should avoid per-node high-cardinality metric labels; store per-node detail in DB + logs/traces, aggregate for metrics.
- Prefer idempotent writes for orchestrator/agent.

Base path (placeholder)
- /internal/fleet-readiness/v1


Endpoints (proto)

1) Get node readiness (for console drilldown + orchestrator reads)
GET /internal/fleet-readiness/v1/nodes/{node_id}

Response (example)
{
  "node_id": "nrn_01J9S8P4Q0C2Y7R2K9J0Q2Z7F1",
  "provider_instance_id": "i-0abc123def456",
  "cluster_id": "clu_us-east-1_prod_01",
  "pool_id": "ded_pool_8f3c1",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "gpu_type": "a100-80gb",
  "image_channel": "candidate",
  "image_version": "gpu-ubuntu2204-nvidia-550.54.14-cuda12.4-2025.10.02",
  "current_state": "Validating",
  "state_updated_at": "2025-10-07T19:02:11Z",
  "state_version": 17,
  "last_validation_run_id": "vrn_01J9S8R06Y3YV9QK0Y9A7M7T8Z",
  "last_failure": null
}

Notes
- last_failure should be included even if state transitions away (e.g., show “recovered from …”?) TBD.


2) List nodes by pool/state (for internal console table views)
GET /internal/fleet-readiness/v1/nodes?pool_id=…&state=Validating&limit=200&cursor=…

Response is a list view (pagination)
{
  "items": [
    {
      "node_id": "…",
      "provider_instance_id": "…",
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "gpu_type": "a100-80gb",
      "current_state": "Validating",
      "state_updated_at": "…",
      "last_failure_code": null
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "…"
}

Notes
- For table views we likely only need a reduced projection; avoid pulling validation artifacts by default.


3) Patch readiness state (authoritative transition write)
PATCH /internal/fleet-readiness/v1/nodes/{node_id}/state

Request (example)
{
  "expected_state_version": 17,
  "new_state": "Ready",
  "transition_reason": "postflight_validations_passed",
  "actor": {
    "type": "service",
    "name": "provisioning-orchestrator"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "pool_id": "ded_pool_8f3c1",
    "region": "us-east-1"
  }
}

Response
{
  "node_id": "…",
  "current_state": "Ready",
  "state_updated_at": "…",
  "state_version": 18
}

Notes
- expected_state_version supports optimistic concurrency (avoid dueling writers).
- We need to decide who is allowed to set Quarantined:
  - orchestrator only?
  - validation-agent can request quarantine but control plane decides?
- Ensure we don’t allow “Ready -> Provisioning” unless explicit operator override.


4) Report validation results (from validation agent / orchestrator)
POST /internal/fleet-readiness/v1/validation-runs

Request (example)
{
  "node_id": "nrn_…",
  "trigger": {
    "type": "postflight",
    "build_id": "prov_2025-10-07_1901Z_7b9",
    "actor": "node-validation-agent"
  },
  "started_at": "2025-10-07T19:01:02Z",
  "finished_at": "2025-10-07T19:02:10Z",
  "overall_status": "fail",
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "gpu_health",
      "status": "pass",
      "duration_ms": 8123
    },
    {
      "name": "driver_parity",
      "status": "pass",
      "duration_ms": 421
    },
    {
      "name": "kubelet_join",
      "status": "pass",
      "duration_ms": 11955
    },
    {
      "name": "nccl_smoke",
      "status": "fail",
      "duration_ms": 600000,
      "failure": {
        "code": "NCCL_SMOKE_TIMEOUT",
        "message": "NCCL all-reduce timed out (600s) on eth0 fabric",
        "remediation": "quarantine; page networking if >3 nodes in 30m"
      },
      "artifact_ptr": "s3://redwood-internal-validation-artifacts/us-east-1/nrn_…/vrn_…/nccl.log"
    }
  ]
}

Response
{
  "validation_run_id": "vrn_…",
  "persisted": true
}

Notes
- We should validate that artifact_ptr uses an allowlisted bucket/prefix.
- The "failure" object above is nested JSON in payload; that’s fine over the wire, but we should store normalized fields for query + dashboards.
- Open question: do we accept partial results (streaming check-by-check), or only “final” submission? Leaning final-only for v1; streaming makes cardinality and complexity worse.


5) Readiness summary endpoint (for internal UI + ops)
GET /internal/fleet-readiness/v1/summary?pool_id=…&window=1h

Response (example)
{
  "pool_id": "ded_pool_8f3c1",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "counts_by_state": {
    "Allocated": 0,
    "Provisioning": 12,
    "Validating": 5,
    "Ready": 128,
    "Quarantined": 3
  },
  "top_failure_codes": [
    {"code": "NCCL_SMOKE_TIMEOUT", "count": 2},
    {"code": "DRIVER_MISMATCH", "count": 1}
  ],
  "updated_at": "2025-10-07T19:03:01Z"
}

Notes
- counts_by_state is “hot path” for UI refresh; cache aggressively.
- Avoid returning per-node IDs in summary.


Event schema (proto)
We likely need a compact event stream for:
- SLO toolkit time-to-ready calculations
- audit trail for state changes (esp. quarantine + image channel changes)
- lightweight integrations (incident bot templates / auto-ticketing)

Option A (preferred for now): publish to internal event bus (or just append-only table + export).

Event: readiness.state_changed
{
  "event_type": "readiness.state_changed",
  "event_id": "evt_01J9S8S3Y2…",
  "emitted_at": "2025-10-07T19:02:11Z",
  "node_id": "nrn_…",
  "pool_id": "ded_pool_8f3c1",
  "cluster_id": "clu_us-east-1_prod_01",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "gpu_type": "a100-80gb",
  "from_state": "Validating",
  "to_state": "Ready",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "actor_name": "provisioning-orchestrator",
  "reason": "postflight_validations_passed",
  "state_version": 18
}

Event: readiness.validation_run_completed
{
  "event_type": "readiness.validation_run_completed",
  "event_id": "evt_…",
  "emitted_at": "…",
  "validation_run_id": "vrn_…",
  "node_id": "nrn_…",
  "pool_id": "ded_pool_…",
  "overall_status": "fail",
  "top_failure_code": "NCCL_SMOKE_TIMEOUT",
  "duration_ms": 68000
}

Event: readiness.node_quarantined (optional convenience event)
{
  "event_type": "readiness.node_quarantined",
  "event_id": "evt_…",
  "emitted_at": "…",
  "node_id": "nrn_…",
  "pool_id": "…",
  "code": "GPU_ECC_HIGH",
  "message": "Uncorrectable ECC error rate above threshold",
  "requested_by": "node-validation-agent"
}

Notes
- SLO toolkit primarily needs timestamps for:
  - allocated_at (source = capacity allocator / terraform apply?)
  - first_joined_cluster_at (kubelet join)
  - validating_started_at
  - ready_at
- We should settle “allocated_at” definition; infra thread is still debating whether it’s cloud instance “running” timestamp vs “capacity allocated in internal system”.


Authz + safety
- Read-only endpoints: internal-console, SRE tooling.
- Write endpoints:
  - PATCH state: provisioning-orchestrator, operator tooling (break-glass).
  - POST validation run: node-validation-agent (DaemonSet) + provisioning-orchestrator.
- Must log audit events for:
  - manual overrides
  - state changes into/out of Quarantined
  - image_channel/version changes for a pool (out of scope here, but relates)


Integration notes (who calls what)

Provisioning Orchestrator
- Calls PATCH /state to move Allocated -> Provisioning, and Provisioning -> Validating.
- Triggers validation agent (or waits for it) and then PATCH /state to Ready if the gate passes.
- If validation fails repeatedly and retry budget exceeded (ENG-4825), orchestrator patches Quarantined w/ failure code.

Node Validation Agent (DaemonSet)
- Runs checks locally; uploads logs to artifact store; submits POST /validation-runs.
- Should include “build_id” and “image_version” in trigger metadata for correlation.

Internal Ops Console
- Uses GET /summary for pool page.
- Uses GET /nodes?pool_id=…&state=… for filtered tables.
- Uses GET /nodes/{id} drilldown.
- Future: operator action buttons (Drain, Reimage, Retry validation) should fan out to the right systems; console should not directly ssh into nodes.

SLO Toolkit / Observability
- Subscribes to readiness.state_changed events.
- Computes “time-to-ready” from Allocated (or Provisioning started) -> Ready.
- Important: event tags must not include node_id in metrics labels (we already got burned by this elsewhere; keep node_id only in logs/traces).


Open questions / TODO
- Decide on canonical node_id format and where it is minted (control plane vs orchestrator).
- Do we need a separate endpoint to “attach” provider_instance_id to node_id (for cases where we allocate then later know the instance id)?
- How do we represent “Ready but capacity withheld” (e.g., Ready but not admitted to serving pool due to rollout flag)?
  - Maybe separate boolean: serving_admitted (later) or separate state “Staged”. ADR currently doesn’t include it.
- Should validation runs be immutable? (yes) How do we handle reruns? (new validation_run_id; point last_validation_run_id to latest)
- Failure codes taxonomy: keep small; align with runbook sections.
- Retention: how long do we retain per-check artifacts? (SRE says shorter for logs, longer for aggregated failure counts)

Notes from Slack alignment (rough)
- Ethan: prefer current-state table + append-only events, not pure event-sourcing.
- Jordan: state transitions must be constrained (no illegal edges), enforce at service layer.
- Vanessa: need failure reasons actionable; “fail” alone causes too many manual pings.

Next steps
- Confirm endpoint names + fields with Infra and SRE.
- Create a minimal OpenAPI spec from this doc (even if we don’t publish it widely).
- Align on “allocated_at” definition for SLI.
